title: Constellation admin shim and chaos-tolerant replay harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight runtime shim (Constellation) that adapts legacy admin utilities and ad-hoc shelllets into the new runbooks-as-tasks execution model. The shim must be able to: 1) wrap existing scripts and idempotent CLIs, 2) record deterministic inputs and side effects for replay, 3) attach structured telemetry and provenance metadata (actor, token-scopes, timing), and 4) run in a chaos-tolerant dry-run and replay harness for incident rehearsal and post-incident validation. This ticket covers design, an initial prototype, integration tests, and a canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Shim can wrap at least three canonical admin utilities (kubectl wrapper, db-migrate helper, support-dump) and expose them as typed runbook tasks
Execution logs include structured provenance fields: actor, auth-method, token-id (redacted), input-hash, output-hash, and execution-duration
Replay mode can deterministically re-run a recorded task sequence in a sandboxed environment with toggles for network/side-effect stubs
Telemetry events are emitted to ops-telemetry with sampling controls and link back to runbook id and trace id
Canary rollout to 10% of org-owned runbook executions with automatic rollback on policy violations or non-idempotent detection
notes: Prototype should be implemented as a small Go binary + shimmed container entrypoint to simplify on-prem deployments
Prefer an interface that uses a single JSONL metadata file per task execution (avoids embedding metadata into stdout)
We will not block on full RBAC surface for MVP; leverage existing auth headers and record them, enforce stricter RBAC in a follow-up
Keep binary < 6MB after strip and upx to ensure quick cold starts for ephemeral debug containers
decisions: Runtime approach: chosen shim + container entrypoint instead of sidecar to reduce orchestration complexity and avoid long-lived processes
State capture: record inputs and exit-code/outputs; not persisting arbitrary filesystem snapshots for MVP (risk trade-off to keep storage bounded)
Idempotency detection: implement heuristics (exit codes, non-deterministic output patterns) and flag suspected non-idempotent tasks during CI rather than blocking rollout
Replay safety: replay runs in a VPC-isolated sandbox with network stub toggles. For sensitive tasks, require explicit "allow-replay" label and human approval
